items.name: Cubanelle
items.fact: Cubanelles are a favorite frying pepper in Cuban and Italian cooking.

scales.name: Melting point
scales.question: The temperature where each one turns to liquid.

items.name: Silver
items.fact: Silver conducts electricity and heat better than any other metal.

items.name: Titanium
items.fact: Titanium is as strong as some steels but about 45% lighter.

items.name: Cocoa butter (chocolate)
items.fact: Chocolate is designed to melt just below body temperature.

items.name: Tin
items.fact: Tin's low melting point made it ideal for solder.

items.name: Table salt
items.fact: Molten salt is used to store heat in some solar power plants.

scales.name: Capital city population
scales.question: People living in the city itself (not the wider metro area). Each gridline step is ten times more.

items.name: Berlin (Germany)
items.fact: Berlin is the #29 most populous of 203 national capitals.

items.name: Monaco
items.fact: Monaco is the #181 most populous of 203 national capitals.

items.name: Vaduz (Liechtenstein)
items.fact: Vaduz is the #197 most populous of 203 national capitals.

items.name: Thimphu (Bhutan)
items.fact: Thimphu is the #168 most populous of 203 national capitals.

items.name: Washington, D.C. (United States)
items.fact: Washington, D.C. is the #115 most populous of 203 national capitals.

scales.name: Voltage
scales.question: How much electrical tension? Each gridline step is ten times more.

items.name: USB phone charger
items.fact: USB has carried 5 volts since the first version in 1996.

items.name: AA battery
items.fact: AAA, AA, C and D alkaline batteries all give the same 1.5 V; bigger ones just last longer.

items.name: Brain waves (EEG) at the scalp
items.fact: Brain waves are measured in millionths of a volt.

items.name: London Underground track
items.fact: Many Tube lines use two live rails, one positive and one negative.

items.name: European wall socket
items.fact: North America uses about 120 V; most of the rest of the world uses 220–240 V.

scales.name: How sweet?
scales.question: Sweetness compared with table sugar (sugar = 1). Each gridline step is ten times sweeter.

items.name: Stevia
items.fact: Stevia sweeteners come from the leaves of a South American plant.

items.name: Fructose (fruit sugar)
items.fact: Fructose is the sweetest natural sugar.

items.name: Saccharin
items.fact: Saccharin, from 1879, is the oldest artificial sweetener.

items.name: Sorbitol
items.fact: Sorbitol is common in sugar-free chewing gum.

items.name: Monellin (berry protein)
items.fact: Monellin is a sweet protein from a West African berry.

scales.name: Boiling point
scales.question: The temperature where each one boils, at normal air pressure.

items.name: Water
items.fact: On top of Mount Everest water boils at only about 70 °C.

items.name: Sulfur
items.fact: Sulfur has been known since ancient times as brimstone.

items.name: Hydrogen
items.fact: Liquid hydrogen fuels many rocket upper stages.

items.name: Iron
items.fact: Iron vapor has been detected in the atmosphere of a scorching exoplanet.

items.name: Aluminium
items.fact: Aluminium stays liquid across a range of almost 1,800 °C.

scales.name: Distance from the Sun
scales.question: Average distance from the Sun in astronomical units (1 AU is Earth's distance). Each gridline step is ten times farther.

items.name: Venus
items.fact: A day on Venus is longer than its year.

items.name: Sedna
items.fact: One orbit of Sedna takes over 11,000 years.

items.name: Ceres
items.fact: Ceres was called a planet for about 50 years after its discovery in 1801.

items.name: Pluto
items.fact: Pluto hasn't completed an orbit since it was discovered in 1930.

items.name: Mercury
items.fact: A year on Mercury lasts 88 Earth days.

scales.name: Lifespan
scales.question: Typical (or record) life length, from hours to millennia.

items.name: Rougheye rockfish (record)
items.fact: Rockfish ages are counted from growth rings in their ear bones.

items.name: Methuselah bristlecone pine
items.fact: Methuselah's exact location is kept secret to protect it.

items.name: House mouse (in captivity)
items.fact: Mice can squeeze through gaps about the width of a pencil.

items.name: Cat
items.fact: The oldest cat on record lived to 38.

items.name: Brandt's bat (record)
items.fact: This tiny bat weighs about 7 g but can live over 40 years.

scales.name: How tall
scales.question: Height from base to top, in meters. Each gridline step is ten times taller.

items.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
items.fact: The tower started leaning during construction, in the 12th century.

items.name: Adult giraffe
items.fact: A giraffe's neck has seven vertebrae, the same as yours.

items.name: Empire State Building (to tip)
items.fact: The Empire State Building gets its own ZIP code.

items.name: Space Needle
items.fact: The Space Needle was built for the 1962 World's Fair.

items.name: Table Mountain
items.fact: Table Mountain is one of the oldest mountains in the world.

scales.name: How heavy?
scales.question: Mass, from milligrams to millions of tonnes. Each gridline step is ten times heavier.

items.name: One-euro coin
items.fact: A one-euro coin is made of two different metal alloys.

items.name: Passenger car
items.fact: Electric cars are usually heavier because of their batteries.

items.name: Argentinosaurus
items.fact: Argentinosaurus is among the largest dinosaurs known.

items.name: General Sherman tree (trunk)
items.fact: General Sherman, a giant sequoia, is the largest living tree by trunk volume.

items.name: Men's shot put
items.fact: The men's shot weighs 7.26 kg, the women's 4 kg.

scales.name: Radiation dose
scales.question: Effective dose in sieverts (Sv). Each gridline step is ten times more.

items.name: Eating a banana
items.fact: Bananas are slightly radioactive because they contain potassium-40.

items.name: Dental X-rays
items.fact: A set of dental X-rays is about the same as a day of natural background radiation.

items.name: Six-month trip to Mars
items.fact: Cosmic rays are very hard to shield against on the way to Mars.

items.name: A year of natural background radiation
items.fact: Radon gas seeping from the ground is the largest single source of natural background radiation.

items.name: Full-body CT scan
items.fact: A full-body CT scan equals several years of natural background radiation.

scales.name: Surface gravity
scales.question: How hard you'd be pulled down standing on each world. Each gridline step is ten times stronger.

items.name: Pluto
items.fact: On Pluto you could jump about 16 times higher than on Earth.

items.name: Triton
items.fact: Triton orbits Neptune backwards and is slowly spiraling inward.

items.name: The Moon
items.fact: Moon gravity is about one-sixth of Earth's.

items.name: Europa
items.fact: Europa likely hides a salty ocean under its ice.

items.name: Saturn
items.fact: Saturn is less dense than water.

scales.name: Earthquake magnitude
scales.question: Moment magnitude. Each whole step releases about 32 times more energy.

items.name: Nepal, 2015
items.fact: The Nepal quake triggered a deadly avalanche on Mount Everest.

items.name: L'Aquila, 2009
items.fact: Six Italian scientists were convicted (later acquitted) over their risk statements before this quake.

items.name: Chile (Maule), 2010
items.fact: It shifted the city of Concepción about 3 m to the west.

items.name: Indian Ocean, 2004
items.fact: Its tsunami reached the coast of Africa, about 5,000 km away.

items.name: Haiti, 2010
items.fact: The 2010 Haiti quake is among the deadliest ever recorded.

scales.name: Energy density
scales.question: Calories (kcal) in 100 grams of each.

items.name: Banana
items.fact: Bananas are slightly radioactive because of their potassium.

items.name: Peanut butter
items.fact: Peanuts are legumes, related to beans and peas.

items.name: Carrot
items.fact: The first cultivated carrots were purple and yellow, not orange.

items.name: Broccoli
items.fact: Broccoli was bred from wild cabbage.

items.name: Apple
items.fact: There are thousands of apple varieties.

scales.name: pH
scales.question: How acidic or basic is it? 7 is neutral; every step down is ten times more acidic.

items.name: Household ammonia
items.fact: Never mix ammonia with bleach: together they release toxic gas.

items.name: Human blood
items.fact: Blood pH outside about 7.35–7.45 is a medical emergency.

items.name: Vinegar
items.fact: Vinegar is mostly water with about 5–8% acetic acid.

items.name: Black coffee
items.fact: Dark roasts are usually slightly less acidic than light roasts.

items.name: Gastric acid
items.fact: Your stomach lining replaces itself every few days to survive its own acid.

scales.name: River length
scales.question: Length from source to mouth in kilometers. Each gridline step is ten times longer.

items.name: Shannon
items.fact: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland and Britain.

items.name: Jordan
items.fact: The Jordan flows into the Dead Sea, the lowest place on land.

items.name: Rhine
items.fact: The Rhine flows through or along six countries.

items.name: Danube
items.fact: The Danube passes through more countries than any other river: ten.

items.name: Amazon
items.fact: The Amazon carries more water than the next seven largest rivers combined.

scales.name: Mohs hardness
scales.question: Which scratches which? 1 is soft as talc, 10 is diamond.

items.name: Corundum (ruby, sapphire)
items.fact: Ruby and sapphire are the same mineral, corundum, colored by different traces of metal.

items.name: Zinc
items.fact: Most modern 'copper' pennies in the US are mostly zinc inside.

items.name: Talc
items.fact: Talc is the softest mineral on the scale and the main ingredient of talcum powder.

items.name: Chromium
items.fact: Chromium is the hardest pure metal, which is why it's used for plating.

items.name: Silicon
items.fact: Silicon wafers for computer chips are cut from huge single crystals.

scales.name: Loudness
scales.question: Sound pressure level in decibels. Every +10 dB sounds roughly twice as loud.

items.name: Krakatoa eruption, 165 km away
items.fact: The 1883 Krakatoa eruption was heard nearly 5,000 km away.

items.name: Chainsaw (1 m)
items.fact: Chainsaw operators are required to wear ear protection.

items.name: Trumpet (0.5 m)
items.fact: A trumpet up close is as loud as the threshold of pain.

items.name: Vacuum cleaner
items.fact: 85 dB over long periods can damage hearing.

items.name: A very calm room
items.fact: A quiet bedroom at night is around 25 dB.

scales.name: What wind force is this?
scales.question: The Beaufort scale describes wind by what you can see it doing, from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane force).

items.name: Twigs break off trees
items.fact: Force 8 is a 'gale'.

items.name: Wind felt on your face; leaves rustle
items.fact: Force 2 is a 'light breeze'.

items.name: Trees uprooted; considerable damage to buildings
items.fact: Force 10, a 'storm', is seldom experienced inland.

items.name: Sea completely white with driving spray
items.fact: Force 12 is 'hurricane force': 118 km/h or more.

items.name: Whole trees in motion; hard to walk against the wind
items.fact: Force 7 is a 'near gale'.

scales.name: When was it completed?
scales.question: The year each landmark was finished or opened.

items.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
items.fact: The current Golden Pavilion is a 1955 rebuild after an arson attack.

items.name: CN Tower
items.fact: The CN Tower is hit by lightning about 75 times a year.

items.name: Empire State Building
items.fact: The Empire State Building took just 410 days to build.

items.name: Brooklyn Bridge
items.fact: P. T. Barnum walked 21 elephants across the Brooklyn Bridge to prove it was safe.

items.name: Golden Gate Bridge
items.fact: The bridge's color is called International Orange.

scales.name: Running time
scales.question: How long each film is, in minutes.

items.name: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937)
items.fact: Snow White was Disney's first feature-length film.

items.name: Barbie (2023)
items.fact: Barbie was the highest-grossing film of 2023.

items.name: Lawrence of Arabia (1962)
items.fact: Lawrence of Arabia has no speaking roles for women.

items.name: Avatar (2009)
items.fact: Avatar is the highest-grossing film of all time.

items.name: The Godfather (1972)
items.fact: Marlon Brando stuffed his cheeks for his audition.

scales.name: How deep down
scales.question: Meters below the water surface. Each gridline step is ten times deeper.

items.name: Lake Tahoe (deepest point)
items.fact: Lake Tahoe is so clear you can see down about 20 m.

items.name: Cuvier's beaked whale dive
items.fact: One Cuvier's beaked whale stayed under for 3 hours 42 minutes.

items.name: Kursk submarine wreck
items.fact: The Kursk sank in the Barents Sea in 2000.

items.name: Challenger Deep
items.fact: The pressure in Challenger Deep is over 1,000 times that at the surface.

items.name: Lake Baikal (deepest point)
items.fact: Lake Baikal holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh water.

scales.name: How much does the sting hurt?
scales.question: Schmidt sting pain index: entomologist Justin Schmidt rated the pain of insect stings he received, from 1 (mild) to 4 (excruciating).

items.name: Potter wasp
items.fact: One of the few stings Schmidt rated below 1.

items.name: Bald-faced hornet
items.fact: Schmidt: "Similar to getting your hand mashed in a revolving door."

items.name: Red paper wasp
items.fact: Schmidt: "Like spilling a beaker of hydrochloric acid on a paper cut."

items.name: Trap-jaw ant
items.fact: Trap-jaw ants snap their jaws shut faster than almost any other animal movement.

items.name: Red fire ant
items.fact: Schmidt: "Like walking across a shag carpet and reaching for the light switch."

scales.name: Country size
scales.question: Land and water area in square kilometers. Each gridline step is ten times bigger.

items.name: Nauru
items.fact: Nauru is the #195 largest of 197 countries by area.

items.name: Monaco
items.fact: Monaco is the #196 largest of 197 countries by area.

items.name: Turkey
items.fact: Turkey is the #38 largest of 197 countries by area.

items.name: Albania
items.fact: Albania is the #140 largest of 197 countries by area.

items.name: Greece
items.fact: Greece is the #97 largest of 197 countries by area.

scales.name: How fast?
scales.question: Top or typical speed in km/h. Each gridline step is ten times faster.

items.name: Light
items.fact: Nothing travels faster than light in a vacuum.

items.name: Peregrine falcon (dive)
items.fact: The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal on Earth.

items.name: Fastest roller coaster (Formula Rossa)
items.fact: Formula Rossa in Abu Dhabi hits 240 km/h in under 5 seconds.

items.name: Speed of sound in air
items.fact: The speed of sound depends on air temperature.

items.name: Airliner cruising
items.fact: An Airbus A380 cruises at about 900 km/h.

scales.name: Caffeine
scales.question: Milligrams of caffeine per serving.

items.name: Unsweetened cocoa powder (100 g)
items.fact: Cocoa powder is where chocolate's caffeine comes from.

items.name: Milk chocolate (100 g)
items.fact: Chocolate also contains theobromine, a milder relative of caffeine.

items.name: Yerba mate (6 g of leaves)
items.fact: Yerba mate is traditionally sipped through a metal straw from a gourd.

items.name: Drip coffee (207 ml)
items.fact: Filter coffee is one of the strongest everyday caffeine sources.

items.name: Diet Coke (330 ml can)
items.fact: Diet Coke has more caffeine than regular Coke.

scales.name: How thick and gooey?
scales.question: Viscosity in millipascal-seconds (water is about 1). Each gridline step is ten times thicker.

items.name: Glycerine
items.fact: Glycerine is used to make soap bubbles last longer.

items.name: Pitch (tar)
items.fact: In the Pitch Drop Experiment, running since 1927, a drop falls about once a decade.

items.name: Ketchup
items.fact: Ketchup gets runnier when you shake it (it's 'shear-thinning').

items.name: Water
items.fact: Water's viscosity drops by half between 20 °C and 50 °C.

items.name: Castor oil
items.fact: Castor oil was once a common household remedy.

scales.name: How much data?
scales.question: Size in bytes. Each gridline step is ten times more.

items.name: A 500-page book as plain text
items.fact: Plain text is tiny: a whole novel fits in under a megabyte.

items.name: Blu-ray disc
items.fact: Blu-ray uses a blue-violet laser with a shorter wavelength than DVD's red one.

items.name: Human memory (Kurzweil's estimate)
items.fact: Futurist Ray Kurzweil estimated a human's functional memory at about 1.25 TB.

items.name: Library of Congress collection (2005)
items.fact: The Library of Congress is the largest library in the world.

items.name: Audio CD
items.fact: A CD holds about 650 MiB, roughly 74 minutes of music.
